title: Glenn Maxwell Retires From International Cricket, Ending 286-Match Australia Career
excerpt: The 38-year-old all-rounder, a three-time World Cup winner, will keep playing T20 franchise cricket for Melbourne Stars after calling time on internationals, first-class and List A cricket.
body:
• Glenn Maxwell, 38, has retired from international cricket, and is also walking away from first-class and List A cricket.
  • He finishes with 286 internationals for Australia — 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Tests — including two ODI World Cup titles and the 2021 T20 World Cup.
  • His last match for Australia was against Oman at the 2026 T20 World Cup in February, where he took two wickets and did not bat.
  • Maxwell will keep playing T20 franchise cricket, with a Melbourne Stars contract in the Big Bash League running to the 2027-28 season.

Glenn Maxwell has retired from international cricket. The 38-year-old Australian all-rounder announced the decision on the Final Word podcast, and is also calling time on first-class cricket and the List A game, according to ESPNcricinfo. He had already quit one-day internationals in June last year, but had kept himself available for T20Is until now.

Maxwell played the T20 World Cup in 2026, where Australia were unable to progress past the group stages. Australia's final match of that tournament, against Oman in February, becomes the last game he played for his country — he picked up two wickets with the ball and did not bat, Cricket.com.au reported.

Why now

Maxwell said he had held a small hope of a farewell appearance at his home ground, the Melbourne Cricket Ground, in Australia's upcoming series against England, but understood the selectors' turn towards youth. "I suppose [I had] a small hope that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG. But I can completely understand the direction they're going with this [T20] squad," he said on the podcast, as reported by Sky Sports.

"There's going to be a lot of change over the next 12 to 24 months with the Olympics coming up [in 2028], and they've got to make sure they get their eyeballs on a few young guys coming through."

— Glenn Maxwell, on the Final Word podcast

He also said telling his Victoria team-mates that his last one-day game for the state was behind him was harder than he expected. "It's probably a time where I probably need to spend a little bit more time investing in the body to make sure I can get through the remaining couple of tournaments I've got in my career," he said, according to ESPNcricinfo. He will manage his knee to be ready for the Big Bash League, with the Stars' opening match on December 18 against Adelaide at the MCG, Cricket.com.au reported.

The record

Maxwell played 130 T20Is for Australia and scored 2,897 runs at a strike rate of 154.42, with 51 wickets, according to ESPNcricinfo. He leaves T20I cricket as Australia's third-highest run-scorer in the format, behind David Warner and Aaron Finch, and as one of only two batters — alongside India's Rohit Sharma — to have scored five T20I centuries, Cricket.com.au reported.

Across 286 international matches he scored more than 7,000 runs and took 136 wickets, Sky Sports reported. He was capped seven times in Test cricket, the last of which came in 2017, and picked up 339 runs with a best of 104 against India in Ranchi, according to ESPNcricinfo.

His most memorable innings came in the format he left first. During the 2023 ODI World Cup he plundered a match-winning 201 not out from 128 balls against Afghanistan while battling injury, as Australia recovered from 91 for 7 to reach a target of 292, Sky Sports reported. He won two ODI World Cups, in 2015 and 2023, and hit the winning runs when Australia were crowned T20 world champions in 2021.

What is next

Maxwell remains available for the Melbourne Stars in the BBL, having had his contract extended to the 2027-28 season, and has remained active on the franchise circuit — he led Belfast Wolves to the final of the inaugural European T20 Premier League in September, according to ESPNcricinfo. For Australia, the immediate focus is the white-ball series against England later this month, which the selectors will now contest with the younger squad Maxwell stepped aside for.
